sanskrit: bhakṣyārtham eva baddhas tvaṃ sa muktaḥ prasṛtaḥ kṣudhā śāstrajñam abhisaṃdhāya nūnaṃ bhakṣayitādya mām
english: It was for the sake of food that you were bound, and once freed you came forth driven by hunger; surely, having outwitted one who knows the treatises, you mean to devour me this very day.

sanskrit: jānāmi kṣudhitaṃ hi tvām āhārasamayaś ca te sa tvaṃ mām abhisaṃdhāya bhakṣyaṃ mṛgayase punaḥ
english: I know that you are hungry, and that this is your hour to feed; and so, having deceived me, you are hunting once more for your prey.

sanskrit: yac cāpi putradāraṃ svaṃ tat saṃnisṛjase mayi śuśrūṣāṃ nāma me kartuṃ sakhe mama na tatkṣamam
english: And as for your offering up your own children and wife to me, professing to render me service—friend, that is not a thing I can permit.

sanskrit: tvayā māṃ sahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā priyā bhāryā sutāś ca ye kasmān māṃ te na khādeyur hṛṣṭāḥ praṇayinas tvayi
english: Seeing me in your company, why would your beloved wife and your sons, devoted and fond of you, not eat me up with delight?

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tvayā sameṣyāmi vṛtto hetuḥ samāgame śivaṃ dhyāyasva me 'trasthaḥ sukṛtaṃ smaryate yadi
english: I will not join with you; the reason for our union has passed. Wish me well from where you stand, if the good deed I did is remembered.

sanskrit: śatror annādyabhūtaḥ san kliṣṭasya kṣudhitasya ca bhakṣyaṃ mṛgayamāṇasya kaḥ prājño viṣayaṃ vrajet
english: What wise creature, being fit to be the food of a foe who is afflicted and famished and on the prowl for prey, would walk into his reach?

sanskrit: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi dūrād api tavodvije nāhaṃ tvayā sameṣyāmi nirvṛto bhava lomaśa
english: May it be well with you—I shall go; even from afar I shrink from you. I will not come together with you; be at peace, O hairy one.

sanskrit: balavat saṃnikarṣo hi na kadā cit praśasyate praśāntād api me prājña bhetavyaṃ balinaḥ sadā
english: Nearness to the strong is never to be commended; even from one who seems calmed, O wise one, the mighty must always be feared.

sanskrit: yadi tv arthena me kāryaṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te kāmaṃ sarvaṃ pradāsyāmi na tv ātmānaṃ kadā cana
english: But if you have need of any object, tell me—what shall I do for you? I will gladly grant you anything, but never my own self.

sanskrit: ātmārthe saṃtatis tyājyā rājyaṃ ratnaṃ dhanaṃ tathā api sarvasvam utsṛjya rakṣed ātmānam ātmanā
english: For one's own sake one must be ready to give up offspring, kingdom, jewels, and wealth; surrendering even all one has, a man should guard his self by his own self.

sanskrit: aiśvaryadhanaratnānāṃ pratyamitre 'pi tiṣṭhatām dṛṣṭā hi punar āvṛttir jīvatām iti naḥ śrutam
english: Of sovereignty, wealth, and jewels, though they pass into a rival's hands, we have seen and heard that for the living there is a getting back again.

sanskrit: na tv ātmanaḥ saṃpradānaṃ dhanaratnavad iṣyate ātmā tu sarvato rakṣyo dārair api dhanair api
english: But the surrender of the self is not, like wealth and jewels, a thing to be desired; the self must be guarded by every means—by wife and by riches alike.

sanskrit: ātmarakṣitatantrāṇāṃ suparīkṣitakāriṇām āpado nopapadyante puruṣāṇāṃ svadoṣajāḥ
english: For men who keep the practice of self-protection and who act only after careful scrutiny, no calamities arise that are born of their own faults.

sanskrit: śatrūn samyag vijānanti durbalā ye balīyasaḥ teṣāṃ na cālyate buddhir ātmārthaṃ kṛtaniścayā
english: Those weak ones who rightly understand their stronger foes—their resolve, fixed for their own sake, is never shaken.

sanskrit: ity abhivyaktam evāsau palitenāvabhartsitaḥ mārjāro vrīḍito bhūtvā mūṣakaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Thus openly upbraided by Palita, the cat, grown ashamed, spoke these words to the mouse:

sanskrit: saṃmanye 'haṃ tava prajñāṃ yas tvaṃ mama hite rataḥ uktavān arthatattvena mayā saṃbhinnadarśanaḥ
english: I honour your wisdom, for you who are devoted to my good have spoken in keeping with the truth of things, though I differ from you in view.

sanskrit: na tu mām anyathā sādho tvaṃ vijñātum ihārhasi prāṇapradānajaṃ tvatto mama sauhṛdam āgatam
english: But you ought not, O good one, to judge me otherwise than as I am: my friendship for you arose from your having granted me my very life.

sanskrit: dharmajño 'smi guṇajño 'smi kṛtajño 'smi viśeṣataḥ mitreṣu vatsalaś cāsmi tvadvidheṣu viśeṣataḥ
english: I know what is right, I know merit, and above all I am grateful; and I am tender toward friends, and toward such as you especially so.

sanskrit: tan mām evaṃgate sādho na yāvayitum arhasi tvayā hi yāvyamāno 'haṃ prāṇāñ jahyāṃ sabāndhavaḥ
english: Therefore, O good one, things being as they are, you ought not to drive me away; if driven off by you, I would give up my life, kinsmen and all.

sanskrit: dhik śabdo hi budhair dṛṣṭo madvidheṣu manasviṣu maraṇaṃ dharmatattvajña na māṃ śaṅkitum arhasi
english: The wise hold that a word of reproach is, for high-minded ones like me, as good as death; you who know the truth of dharma ought not to suspect me.

sanskrit: iti saṃstūyamāno hi mārjāreṇa sa mūṣakaḥ manasā bhāvagambhīraṃ mārjāraṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Being thus flattered by the cat, the mouse, weighing in his mind the cat's deep designs, spoke these words:

sanskrit: sādhur bhavāñ śrutārtho 'smi prīyate na ca viśvase saṃstavair vā dhanaughair vā nāhaṃ śakyaḥ punas tvayā
english: You are a worthy one, and I have heard your case; I am pleased, yet I do not trust. Not by praises, nor by floods of wealth, can I be won over by you again.

sanskrit: na hy amitravaśaṃ yānti prājñā niṣkāraṇaṃ sakhe asminn arthe ca gāthe dve nibodhośanasā kṛte
english: For the wise do not fall under a foe's power without cause, my friend; and on this matter mark the two verses composed by Uśanas:

sanskrit: śatrusādhāraṇe kṛtye kṛtvā saṃdhiṃ balīyasā samāhitaś cared yuktyā kṛtārthaś ca na viśvaset
english: In a task common to oneself and an enemy, having made a pact with the stronger, one should act warily and with skill; and once the end is gained, one should not trust.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu rakṣej jīvitam ātmanaḥ dravyāṇi saṃtatiś caiva sarvaṃ bhavati jīvataḥ
english: Therefore in every condition one should guard one's own life; for goods and offspring and all besides belong only to the living.

sanskrit: saṃkṣepo nītiśāstrāṇām aviśvāsaḥ paro mataḥ nṛṣu tasmād aviśvāsaḥ puṣkalaṃ hitam ātmanaḥ
english: The sum of the treatises on policy is held to be supreme distrust toward men; hence distrust is an abundant blessing to oneself.

sanskrit: vadhyante na hy aviśvastāḥ śatrubhir durbalā api viśvastās tv āśu vadhyante balavanto 'pi durbalaiḥ
english: The distrustful, even though weak, are not slain by their foes; but the trustful, even though strong, are swiftly slain by the weak.

sanskrit: tvadvidhebhyo mayā hy ātmā rakṣyo mārjāra sarvadā rakṣa tvam api cātmānaṃ caṇḍālāj jātikilbiṣāt
english: From such as you, O cat, my self must always be guarded; and you too should guard your self from that low-born outcast of polluted birth.

sanskrit: sa tasya bruvatas tv evaṃ saṃtrāsāj jātasādhvasaḥ svabilaṃ hi javenāśu mārjāraḥ prayayau tataḥ
english: While the mouse was speaking thus, the cat, seized with sudden dread, fled at once in haste to his own den.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāstrārthatattvajño buddhisāmarthyam ātmanaḥ viśrāvya palitaḥ prājño bilam anyaj jagāma ha
english: Then Palita, the wise one who knew the true purport of the treatises, having proved the power of his own intelligence, betook himself to another hole.

sanskrit: evaṃ prajñāvatā buddhyā durbalena mahābalāḥ ekena bahavo 'mitrāḥ palitenābhisaṃdhitāḥ
english: Thus by his wise understanding the weak one outwitted the mighty; many foes were outmatched by Palita alone.

sanskrit: ariṇāpi samarthena saṃdhiṃ kurvīta paṇḍitaḥ mūṣakaś ca biḍālaś ca muktāv anyonyasaṃśrayāt
english: Even with a capable enemy the prudent man should make a pact; the mouse and the cat were both delivered by their mutual reliance.

sanskrit: ity eṣa kṣatradharmasya mayā mārgo 'nudarśitaḥ vistareṇa mahīpāla saṃkṣepeṇa punaḥ śṛṇu
english: Thus have I shown you at length the path of the kṣatriya's duty, O lord of earth; now hear it once more in brief.

sanskrit: anyonyakṛtavairau tu cakratuḥ prītim uttamām anyonyam abhisaṃdhātum abhūc caiva tayor matiḥ
english: Though they had made enmity with each other, the two formed a perfect friendship; yet the mind of each was set on outwitting the other.

sanskrit: tatra prājño 'bhisaṃdhatte samyag buddhibalāśrayāt abhisaṃdhīyate prājñaḥ pramādād api cābudhaiḥ
english: In such a case the wise one prevails by relying rightly on the strength of his wit; but a wise man may be outdone, through heedlessness, even by fools.

sanskrit: tasmād abhītavad bhīto viśvastavad aviśvasan na hy apramattaś calati calito vā vinaśyati
english: Therefore, though fearful, let him bear himself as fearless; though distrustful, as one who trusts. For the vigilant man is not unseated, nor, once unseated, does he perish.

sanskrit: kālena ripuṇā saṃdhiḥ kāle mitreṇa vigrahaḥ kārya ity eva tattvajñāḥ prāhur nityaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: In season, peace even with a foe; in season, strife even with a friend—this, those who know the truth ever declare must be done, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: evaṃ matvā mahārāja śāstrārtham abhigamya ca abhiyukto 'pramattaś ca prāg bhayād bhītavac caret
english: Reflecting thus, O great king, and grasping the meaning of the treatises, let him remain intent and vigilant, and act as one afraid before danger comes.

sanskrit: bhītavat saṃvidhiḥ kāryaḥ pratisaṃdhis tathaiva ca bhayād utpadyate buddhir apramattābhiyogajā
english: His arrangements and his counter-arrangements alike should be made as by one in fear; for from fear arises the discernment that is born of unremitting effort.

sanskrit: na bhayaṃ vidyate rājan bhītasyānāgate bhaye abhītasya tu visrambhāt sumahaj jāyate bhayam
english: For one who fears before danger comes, O king, no danger arises; but for the fearless, through his confidence, a very great danger is born.

sanskrit: na bhīrur iti cātyantaṃ mantro 'deyaḥ kathaṃ cana avijñānād dhi vijñāte gacched āspadadarśiṣu
english: Yet counsel must never be wholly withheld from a man on the grounds that he is timid; for through such a misjudgement, knowledge passes from the ignorant to those who watch for an opening.

sanskrit: tasmād abhītavad bhīto viśvastavad aviśvasan kāryāṇāṃ gurutāṃ buddhvā nānṛtaṃ kiṃ cid ācaret
english: Therefore, though afraid, bearing himself as fearless, and though distrustful, as one who trusts, let him weigh the gravity of his affairs and never practise any falsehood.

sanskrit: evam etan mayā proktam itihāsaṃ yudhiṣṭhira śrutvā tvaṃ suhṛdāṃ madhye yathāvat samupācara
english: Thus has this old tale been told by me, O Yudhiṣṭhira; having heard it, conduct yourself fittingly in the midst of your friends.

sanskrit: upalabhya matiṃ cāgryām arimitrāntaraṃ tathā saṃdhivigrahakālaṃ ca mokṣopāyaṃ tathāpadi
english: Having attained the highest wisdom, and the difference between foe and friend, and the seasons for peace and for war, and the means of deliverance in calamity—

sanskrit: śatrusādhāraṇe kṛtye kṛtvā saṃdhiṃ balīyasā samāgamaṃ cared yuktyā kṛtārtho na ca viśvaset
english: in a task shared with an enemy, having made a pact with the stronger, let him conduct the alliance with skill, and, once his end is gained, not trust.

sanskrit: aviruddhāṃ trivargeṇa nītim etāṃ yudhiṣṭhira abhyuttiṣṭha śrutād asmād bhūyas tvaṃ rañjayan prajāḥ
english: This policy, not at odds with the three aims of life, O Yudhiṣṭhira—rise up to it after what you have heard, and ever more bring joy to your subjects.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiś cāpi te sārdhaṃ yātrā bhavatu pāṇḍava brāhmaṇā hi paraṃ śreyo divi ceha ca bhārata
english: Let your course be taken together with the brāhmaṇas, O Pāṇḍava; for the brāhmaṇas are the highest good, in heaven and here, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ete dharmasya vettāraḥ kṛtajñāḥ satataṃ prabho pūjitāḥ śubhakarmāṇaḥ pūrvajityā narādhipa
english: These are the knowers of dharma, ever grateful, O lord; honoured and pure in their deeds, they win victory beforehand, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ śreyaḥ paraṃ rājan yaśaḥ kīrtiṃ ca lapsyase kulasya saṃtatiṃ caiva yathānyāyaṃ yathākramam
english: You shall gain a kingdom and the highest good, O king, and glory and renown, and the continuance of your line, each in due right and due order.

sanskrit: dvayor imaṃ bhārata saṃdhivigrahaṃ; subhāṣitaṃ buddhiviśeṣakāritam tathānvavekṣya kṣitipena sarvadā; niṣevitavyaṃ nṛpa śatrumaṇḍale
english: This well-spoken lesson of peace and war between two parties, O Bhārata, wrought by surpassing intelligence—having thus regarded it, a ruler of earth, O king, must ever practise it amid the circle of his foes.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ukto mantro mahābāho na viśvāso 'sti śatruṣu kathaṃ hi rājā varteta yadi sarvatra nāśvaset
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The counsel has been given, O mighty-armed one—that there is no trusting in foes. But how is a king to conduct himself if he can nowhere place his confidence?

sanskrit: viśvāsād dhi paraṃ rājño rājann utpadyate bhayam kathaṃ vai nāśvasan rājā śatrūñ jayati pārthiva
english: From trust, indeed, a king's greatest peril arises, O king; yet how can a king who places no trust conquer his foes, O lord of the earth?

sanskrit: etan me saṃśayaṃ chindhi mano me saṃpramuhyati aviśvāsakathām etām upaśrutya pitāmaha
english: Resolve this doubt of mine; my mind is utterly bewildered, O grandsire, having listened to this discourse on distrust.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu kaunteya yo vṛtto brahmadattaniveśane pūjanyā saha saṃvādo brahmadattasya pārthiva
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, son of Kuntī, what passed in the dwelling of Brahmadatta—the colloquy that Brahmadatta held with Pūjanī, O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: kāmpilye brahmadattasya antaḥpuranivāsinī pūjanī nāma śakunī dīrghakālaṃ sahoṣitā
english: In Kāmpilya there dwelt within the inner apartments of Brahmadatta a bird named Pūjanī, who had lived with him a long while.

sanskrit: rutajñā sarvabhūtānāṃ yathā vai jīvajīvakaḥ sarvajñā sarvadharmajñā tiryagyonigatāpi sā
english: She understood the cries of all creatures, like the jīvajīvaka bird; all-knowing and versed in every duty was she, though born in the brute kind.

sanskrit: abhiprajātā sā tatra putram ekaṃ suvarcasam samakālaṃ ca rājño 'pi devyāḥ putro vyajāyata
english: There she gave birth to a single son of radiant lustre, and at that very same time a son was also born to the king's queen.

sanskrit: samudratīraṃ gatvā sā tv ājahāra phaladvayam puṣṭyarthaṃ ca svaputrasya rājaputrasya caiva ha
english: Going to the shore of the sea, she brought back two fruits, for the nourishment of her own son and of the king's son alike.

sanskrit: phalam ekaṃ sutāyādād rājaputrāya cāparam amṛtāsvādasadṛśaṃ balatejovivardhanam tatrāgacchat parāṃ vṛddhiṃ rājaputraḥ phalāśanāt
english: One fruit she gave to her own son and the other to the prince—a fruit like the taste of the nectar of immortality, increasing strength and splendour; and from eating it the prince attained the utmost growth.

sanskrit: dhātryā hastagataś cāpi tenākrīḍata pakṣiṇā śūnye tu tam upādāya pakṣiṇaṃ samajātakam hatvā tataḥ sa rājendra dhātryā hastam upāgamat
english: Held in the nurse's hands, he would play with that bird; but one day, in a lonely place, taking up the bird that was born at the same time as himself, he killed it, O lord of kings, and then returned to the nurse's hands.

sanskrit: atha sā śakunī rājann āgamat phalahārikā apaśyan nihataṃ putraṃ tena bālena bhūtale
english: Then the bird returned, O king, bringing fruit, and beheld her son slain by that child and lying upon the ground.

sanskrit: bāṣpapūrṇamukhī dīnā dṛṣṭvā sā tu hataṃ sutam pūjanī duḥkhasaṃtaptā rudatī vākyam abravīt
english: Her face full of tears, wretched at seeing her son slain, Pūjanī, scorched with grief and weeping, spoke these words:

sanskrit: kṣatriye saṃgataṃ nāsti na prītir na ca sauhṛdam kāraṇe saṃbhajantīha kṛtārthāḥ saṃtyajanti ca
english: In a kṣatriya there is no fellowship, no affection, and no friendship; for a purpose they cleave to you here, and once their end is gained they cast you off.

sanskrit: kṣatriyeṣu na viśvāsaḥ kāryaḥ sarvopaghātiṣu apakṛtyāpi satataṃ sāntvayanti nirarthakam
english: No trust should be placed in kṣatriyas, who would destroy all alike; even after doing harm they keep soothing you forever, to no purpose.

sanskrit: aham asya karomy adya sadṛśīṃ vairayātanām kṛtaghnasya nṛśaṃsasya bhṛśaṃ viśvāsaghātinaḥ
english: This very day I shall take upon him a fitting vengeance in kind—upon this ingrate, this cruel one, this gross betrayer of trust.

sanskrit: sahasaṃjātavṛddhasya tathaiva sahabhojinaḥ śaraṇāgatasya ca vadhas trividhaṃ hy asya kilbiṣam
english: To slay one born and reared together with you, one who ate beside you, and one who came to you for refuge—threefold is the guilt of this deed.

sanskrit: ity uktvā caraṇābhyāṃ tu netre nṛpasutasya sā bhittvā svasthā tata idaṃ pūjanī vākyam abravīt
english: So saying, with both her claws she tore out the eyes of the king's son, and then, composed once more, Pūjanī spoke these words:

sanskrit: icchayaiva kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ sadya evopasarpati kṛtapratikriyaṃ teṣāṃ na naśyati śubhāśubham
english: A sin done deliberately recoils upon its doer that very moment; for those whose deeds bring their requital, good and evil do not pass away unanswered.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ karma kṛtaṃ kiṃ cin na tasmin yadi vidyate nipātyate 'sya putreṣu na cet pautreṣu naptṛṣu
english: If any evil deed has been done, should its fruit not be found in the doer himself, it falls upon his sons, or, failing that, upon his grandsons and their descendants.

sanskrit: brahmadatta uvāca asti vai kṛtam asmābhir asti pratikṛtaṃ tvayā ubhayaṃ tat samībhūtaṃ vasa pūjani mā gamaḥ
english: Brahmadatta said: A wrong was indeed done by us, and requital has been done by you; the two are now made even. Dwell here, Pūjanī; do not go.

sanskrit: pūjany uvāca sakṛt kṛtāparādhasya tatraiva parilambataḥ na tad budhāḥ praśaṃsanti śreyas tatrāpasarpaṇam
english: Pūjanī said: Where a wrong has once been committed, to linger on in that same place the wise do not commend; better there to slip away.

sanskrit: sāntve prayukte nṛpate kṛtavaire na viśvaset kṣipraṃ prabadhyate mūḍho na hi vairaṃ praśāmyati
english: Though soothing words be employed, O king, one in whom enmity has arisen should not be trusted; the fool is swiftly destroyed, for enmity is not stilled.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ kṛtavairāṇāṃ putrapautraṃ nigacchati putrapautre vinaṣṭe tu paralokaṃ nigacchati
english: Among those who have made enmity with each other, it descends upon sons and grandsons; and when sons and grandsons are destroyed, it follows them into the next world.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ kṛtavairāṇām aviśvāsaḥ sukhāvahaḥ ekāntato na viśvāsaḥ kāryo viśvāsaghātakaḥ
english: For all who have made enmity, distrust brings ease; in no way at all should trust be placed in a destroyer of trust.

sanskrit: na viśvased aviśvaste viśvaste 'pi na viśvaset kāmaṃ viśvāsayed anyān pareṣāṃ tu na viśvaset
english: One should not trust the untrustworthy, nor even the trusted should one trust. Let one freely inspire trust in others, but in others place no trust.

sanskrit: mātā pitā bāndhavānāṃ variṣṭhau; bhāryā jarā bījamātraṃ tu putraḥ bhrātā śatruḥ klinnapāṇir vayasya; ātmā hy ekaḥ sukhaduḥkhasya vettā
english: Mother and father are the best of kinsmen; a wife is but a comrade in old age; a son is no more than one's own seed; a brother is a foe; a friend has a hand that is wet only while you feast—the self alone is the knower of its own joy and sorrow.

sanskrit: anyonyakṛtavairāṇāṃ na saṃdhir upapadyate sa ca hetur atikrānto yadartham aham āvasam
english: Among those who have made enmity with each other no true peace can come about; and that reason for which I dwelt here has now passed away.

sanskrit: pūjitasyārthamānābhyāṃ jantoḥ pūrvāpakāriṇaḥ ceto bhavaty aviśvastaṃ pūrvaṃ trāsayate balāt
english: Even when a creature who has done harm before is honoured with wealth and respect, his mind remains distrustful, for the earlier wrong terrifies him by its own force.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ saṃmānanā yatra paścāc caiva vimānanā jahyāt taṃ sattvavān vāsaṃ saṃmānitavimānitaḥ
english: Where there is honour at first and dishonour afterward, the man of spirit, honoured and then slighted, should abandon that dwelling.

sanskrit: uṣitāsmi tavāgāre dīrghakālam ahiṃsitā tad idaṃ vairam utpannaṃ sukham āssva vrajāmy aham
english: I have dwelt in your house a long while, unharmed; now this enmity has arisen. Fare well—I take my leave.
